_comment: OPERATOR-OWNED MCP manifest (REVISE-2 gate B9). The probe fails the boot when
the generated mcp.json or the live tools/list diverges from THIS file in either
direction: a missing server, an EXTRA server, a destructive tool the manifest
does not expect (new upstream capability -> must be reviewed and denied here
first), or an expected destructive tool that is absent (stale manifest, or the
wrong endpoint answered). destructive lists were enumerated from the LIVE hosted
endpoints on 2026-07-31; the pattern the probe scans live tools with is
built-in tools that must appear in JCODE_TOOLS_DENY, including its `mcp`
management tool (a cycle must not be able to reconfigure its own tool surface).

readchecks (2026-08-02): ONE PROVEN CALL PER SERVER. The old single `readcheck` covered airtable only, which is how Context7 passed every boot for days while never being called once — tools/list proves a handshake, not usability. Context7's own troubleshooting docs say the same: verify with a real request. A server that cannot be read without side effects must carry a written readcheck_exempt reason; an omission now fails the boot.

browseros.readcheck_exempt: drives a real browser shared with the operator's own EKAP/MERSIS sessions; every tool it exposes either navigates or reads a live page, so a boot-time call would touch operator state. Covered instead by the tabs/list call the bridge scripts make.
